memory_candidates.content: For a shell-script lint whose curated-array population is majority-in-scope with few genuine exceptions, follow the EXCLUDED-style convention (a literal bash array of exceptions, each with its own reason comment, plus a mirror is_excluded_from_X() helper) rather than an INCLUDED-style allowlist, a frontmatter-declared opt-in, or a separate registry file. A fail-closed default (iterate the full population, FAIL by name on anything unaccounted for) makes a Check-N-style completeness net unnecessary, since a new population member is in scope the moment it is added.

When widening a lint check to scan a larger population (e.g. removing a content pre-filter so it now iterates every dispatchable file), always re-run EVERY sibling test suite that shares the same lint script, not just the suite directly associated with the changed check. A pre-existing shared 'fully compliant, no FAIL expected' fixture authored before the new/widened check existed can silently regress, because its WORKDIR tree structure (e.g. which extension agents/ directories it happens to create) can incidentally collide with the new check's own scoping logic in ways the original check author never anticipated.

To run a bash test suite against a modified/restored variant of the script it tests (a negative control) without mutating the working tree: copy both the test suite and the script-under-test to a scratch directory, hardcode the copied suite's SCRIPT_DIR variable to the REAL script directory (fragment/lib sourcing is typically SCRIPT_DIR-relative and breaks if the copy lives elsewhere), then override the copied suite's LINT_SRC (or equivalent) to point at the scratch script variant. A plain env-var override does not work when the target script assigns its own var unconditionally (not via ${VAR:-default}).
